idiom_name: withX(Component) higher-order function returning a wrapper component
implementation_notes: This is the pattern's home ground: an enhancer is a plain function Component => Component - React's documentation states that HOCs are not part of the React API but emerge from its compositional nature - so nothing has to be structured, the function simply returns a wrapper component that renders the wrapped one with merged props. Since React 16.8 a custom hook replaces it for new function-component logic (the same behaviour with no extra node, no injected props and no display-name bookkeeping), and the React documentation recommends that form; the enhancer remains the right tool for library APIs that must wrap any component shape (connect, withTranslation, withRouter) and for sharing logic into class components, where hooks cannot be used.
pitfalls: Applying the enhancer inside render creates a new component type on every render, so the subtree unmounts and remounts and its state is lost - apply it at the definition or export site.
Refs and static methods do not pass through the wrapper: use forwardRef (ref is an ordinary prop from React 19) and hoist-non-react-statics rather than assuming they survive.
Injected props collide with parent-passed props of the same name and the spread order silently decides the winner: namespace the injected props or strip them explicitly.
